decisions.executionNote: Board shows a red race car. Begin a continuous elbow-up approach, right arm toward basket handle, left preparing over its own side.
Initial IK step rejected with no movement; reduce all approach increments to establish continuous elbow-up motion.
Continue gradual downward tool rotation and advance right arm toward the moving basket; left stays in left workspace.
Approach above the basket arch and orient right jaws across its handle. Basket is moving rightward; handle depth remains approximate.
Replan with smaller right-arm increments after partial rejection; align above the arch while finishing downward orientation.
Bring right fingertip center over the basket handle crest; keep left stationary and jaws open during alignment.
Reduce orientation and lateral increments, slightly lowering the wrist to avoid the high folded singularity while approaching the handle.
Basket arch appears higher than estimated. Withdraw upward and slightly back to clear it and restore joint-limit margin before grasping.
Upward motion met a reach limit. Retreat backward/down and reduce downward pitch to approach the handle obliquely with extension margin.
Use very small initial retreat increments to leave the near-extension singularity without a joint jump.
No motion on rejected retreat. Further reduce initial increment, then gradually build movement away from extension.
Tilt the right tool toward the arch instead of extending the arm farther, aligning jaw closure across the handle.
Move open right jaws a few centimeters forward and upward toward the visible handle crest, preserving the current continuous configuration.
Close right jaws at the handle region, then make a small backward/upward test lift. Retention must be checked visually.
Basket retention is unclear and handle appears beyond the tips. Reopen and tilt forward/up to re-center the handle before another closure.
Track the basket's rightward motion and close at the handle, then test retention with a small lift.
Keep right jaws closed and lift upward/backward by 8 cm, watching whether basket rises with the gripper.
The prior lift did not retain the basket. Reopen and visually align the jaws slightly right and above the visible handle crest before closing again.
Test the new handle grasp with an 8 cm upward/backward motion, keeping jaws closed. Left arm prepares for the red race car entering from the left.
Basket remains on the belt. Re-approach farther forward and right with open jaws, lowering from the overly high test position and away from the joint-limit region.
Continue the open-jaw depth correction toward the handle; previous pixel alignment was in front of the basket, not a retained grasp.
Forward handle approach reaches an IK limit. Lower and retract slightly to the accessible front rim, keeping elbow-up continuity and open jaws.
Use smaller initial retreat increments after the rejection, then lower toward the front rim with increasing joint margin.
Handle leg is now near the jaw center in the wrist view. Close at this lower accessible segment and make a small inward lift test.
Test the handle-leg grasp with a 10 cm inward/upward lift while bringing the left open gripper closer to the race car without crossing arms.
No basket retention visible. Switch to a lower rim approach with downward-facing jaws and move farther into the right workspace.
Track the near basket rim with the right gripper, finishing its downward orientation. Left approaches the conveyor target from above.
Stop the near-limit rotation and lower with small lateral steps toward the accessible basket rim. Left continues its open approach to the race car.
Left descent met a tracking obstruction; ease upward. Tilt the right tool forward and raise slightly to reach the rim without overextending the arm.
Raise and advance the right jaws toward the nearest basket rim. Make a small left descent and close as the identified race car moves under its jaws.
Reduce right reach demand by drawing the wrist back and tilting forward; left reopens and adjusts toward the race car visible off-center in its wrist view.
Close the centered left jaws on the race-car nose and begin a small test lift. Right jaws advance toward the nearest rim and close for another retention test.
Keep both jaws closed and test retention with a modest car lift and a 9 cm inward basket lift; visually verify both rather than relying on closure state.
Both test lifts were empty. Reopen, lower and track the race car to center its body; right approaches the basket's remaining accessible near rim.
Left wrist shows the car body just ahead of the pinch point; advance a small amount and close without further descent. Right tracks the rim with a shallower reach and closes.
Test the car body grasp with a small vertical lift. Draw the right wrist back from its reach limit while turning toward the remaining basket edge.
No motion occurred on rejection. Reduce the initial right retreat/turn sharply; continue the small closed-jaw car lift only if both IK checks pass.
Car stays fixed between the left jaws during the test lift; raise and stage it within the left workspace. Reopen the right jaws and close around the visible near basket corner.
Hold the visibly retained race car stationary. After the right IK rejection, retreat with very small initial increments and test the latest rim grasp while lifting.
Basket is still unretained. Keep the car secure while taking a shallower, lower right-arm approach to the basket's near edge with open jaws.
Avoid further extension after the rejected step. Turn the right tool toward the visible basket corner while slightly lowering/backing the wrist; keep the car held.
The near basket corner is visible ahead of the open right jaws. Lower toward its rim with very small lateral tracking and maintain the held car.
Wrist view shows the rim above the pinch line after lowering. Correct upward while keeping the horizontal approach and car secure.
Right reach is at its continuity limit. Draw the wrist inward and turn toward a horizontal side grasp to regain configuration margin, retaining the car.
Right wrist now faces the basket side directly. Advance open jaws toward the upper side rim with small forward, lateral and upward corrections; keep the car retained.
After the reach rejection, avoid further extension. Correct right-jaw alignment backward and upward, using the wrist view while keeping the race car securely held.
